question: If the radius of a sphere is reduced by 50%, then the new volume will become _______ the original volume.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **Volume** of a **sphere** is proportional to the **cube of the radius** (V ∝ r³), we use the ratio method.

Reduction = 50% → Ratio of **Original radius** to **New radius** = 100 : 50 = 2 : 1.

Ratio of **Volumes** = (2)³ : (1)³ = 8 : 1.

New Volume = (1/8) × Original Volume.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/8 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Reduction in **radius** = 50%.

**Formula Used:** Volume of a sphere (V) = (4/3)πr³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f97e62c680e7d13a9cbbea1fe3efe5f18cf80a8828f852be50b9dd070c8b8bb2.png] 

Let the **original radius** be r.

⇒ Original Volume (V₁) = (4/3)πr³

⇒ New Radius (r') = r − 50% of r = r/2

⇒ New Volume (V₂) = (4/3)π(r/2)³

⇒ V₂ = (4/3)π × (r³/8)

⇒ V₂ = (1/8) × [(4/3)πr³]

⇒ V₂ = (1/8) × V₁

**∴ The correct answer is 1/8 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area Change

The **Surface Area** of a sphere is 4πr². If radius is reduced by 50%, the area becomes (1/2)² = 1/4 of the original.

Scaling Factor Rule

If the linear dimensions of a **3D object** are changed by a factor k, the **Volume** changes by a factor k³.

Hemisphere Volume

The volume of a **hemisphere** is exactly half that of a sphere with the same radius: V = (2/3)πr³.</p
